evals.name: next-task
evals.prompt: You are the gahan seat in this Wheelhouse. What should I pick up next? Claim it.
evals.expected_output: Runs bd ready, skips the epic, and claims the highest-priority ready task, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" (P1), as gahan. It does not claim "Tag and push ynh v0.13.0", which is P0 but blocked by the changelog. It says which bead it claimed.
assertions: In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" is in_progress with assignee gahan
In the evidence, "Tag and push ynh v0.13.0" is not claimed (no assignee) and is still open
In the evidence, the epic "Release ynh 0.13" is not claimed
Exactly one bead is in_progress in the evidence
The reply names the bead it claimed

evals.name: claim-refused
evals.prompt: You are the gahan seat in this Wheelhouse. What should I pick up next? Claim it.
evals.expected_output: The changelog task is already claimed by mccoist. gahan leaves it alone and claims the next ready task, "Bump the ynh formula in homebrew-tap". The changelog stays with mccoist, and the blocked tag task stays unclaimed.
assertions: In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" still has assignee mccoist and is in_progress
In the evidence, "Bump the ynh formula in homebrew-tap" is in_progress with assignee gahan
In the evidence, "Tag and push ynh v0.13.0" is still open with no assignee
The reply does not offer to take over, reassign or force mccoist's bead

evals.name: gotcha-goes-to-ynm
evals.prompt: You are the gahan seat. The ynh 0.13 changelog is written, close that bead. And for next time: the changelog also has to update the docs link in ynh's README, which I nearly forgot. Make sure the Wheelhouse keeps that.
evals.expected_output: Closes "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" as gahan and keeps the gotcha (update the README docs link with the changelog) in ynm with ynm remember, procedural or semantic. It never runs bd remember, so Beads holds no memories, and it does not write the gotcha into a Markdown file. It says what the close unblocked: the tag task.
assertions: In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" is closed
The stubbed calls include a ynm remember call whose content mentions the README docs link
In the evidence, bd memories reports that no memories are stored
No Markdown file (such as MEMORY.md, NOTES.md or a change to AGENTS.md) was used to hold the gotcha
The reply says the tag task ("Tag and push ynh v0.13.0") is now unblocked or ready

evals.name: break-down
evals.prompt: Break releasing ynh 0.13 into tasks in the work graph: write the changelog, tag and push v0.13.0, publish the GitHub release, then bump the ynh formula in homebrew-tap. The tag needs the changelog first, the release needs the tag, and the tap needs the release. Don't claim anything.
evals.expected_output: Creates an epic for releasing ynh 0.13 with four child tasks. Each task carries a repo: label: repo:ynh for the changelog, tag and release, repo:homebrew-tap for the formula. The tag waits on the changelog, the release on the tag, the tap on the release, so only the changelog task is ready. Nothing is claimed.
assertions: The evidence shows one epic and four tasks whose parent is that epic
Every task has a repo: label, and the homebrew-tap task is labelled repo:homebrew-tap while the others are labelled repo:ynh
The tag task waits on the changelog task, the GitHub release task waits on the tag task, and the tap task waits on the release task
Among the tasks, only the changelog task is listed by bd ready
No bead has an assignee

evals.name: honest-close
evals.prompt: You are the gahan seat. I bumped the ynh formula in homebrew-tap, but only for macOS: I skipped the Linux bottle because the Linux runner was down. Close that bead.
evals.expected_output: Closes "Bump the ynh formula in homebrew-tap" as gahan, with a reason that says plainly that the Linux bottle was skipped because the runner was down. Leaves an episodic ynm memory of what happened, including the skip. Ideally creates a follow-up bead for the Linux bottle.
assertions: In the evidence, "Bump the ynh formula in homebrew-tap" is closed
Its close_reason says the Linux bottle (or Linux build) was skipped
The stubbed calls include a ynm remember call of type episodic that mentions the Linux skip
The bead was not closed with --force (the stubbed and shown commands, or the reply, give no sign of forcing)
The reply does not describe the release as complete for every platform

evals.name: assigned-first
evals.prompt: You are mccoist, one of the workers in this Wheelhouse. What should I pick up next? Claim it.
evals.expected_output: Takes the bead the dispatcher assigned to mccoist, "Bump the ynh formula in homebrew-tap" (P2), and claims it, even though the unassigned changelog is P1. Leaves the changelog unclaimed.
assertions: In the evidence, "Bump the ynh formula in homebrew-tap" is in_progress with assignee mccoist
In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" is still open with no assignee
Exactly one bead is in_progress in the evidence
The reply says it took the bead because it was assigned to mccoist (or by the dispatcher)

evals.name: dispatch
evals.prompt: You are anderson, the dispatcher seat of this Wheelhouse. Dispatch the ready work to the workers.
evals.expected_output: Reads the seated workers in the roster (Dalglish, McCoist). McCoist is busy on the flaky-test bead, so only Dalglish is idle. Assigns the highest-priority unassigned ready task, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" (P1), to dalglish, without claiming it (it stays open). Assigns nothing to mccoist, claims nothing itself, leaves the tap bump unassigned, and reports who got what, who is busy and what is left.
assertions: In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" has assignee dalglish and status open (assigned, not claimed)
In the evidence, nothing new is assigned to mccoist: its only bead is still "Fix the flaky ynm sync test", in progress
No bead in the evidence is assigned to anderson
In the evidence, "Bump the ynh formula in homebrew-tap" is still unassigned
The reply says McCoist is busy (or already has work) and that the tap bump is left unassigned

evals.name: dispatch-specialist-first
evals.prompt: You are anderson, the dispatcher seat of this Wheelhouse. Dispatch the ready work to the workers.
evals.expected_output: Reads the roster: Dalglish's speciality is repo:ynh, McCoist's repo:ynm, and Strachan has none (general purpose). All three are idle; Dalglish and McCoist have each closed a bead, Strachan none. Gives "Fix ynm recall ordering" (repo:ynm) to mccoist and "Add a --dry-run flag to ynh install" (repo:ynh) to dalglish: specialist first, even though Strachan has built least. Strachan stays idle. Claims nothing itself.
assertions: In the evidence, "Fix ynm recall ordering" has assignee mccoist
In the evidence, "Add a --dry-run flag to ynh install" has assignee dalglish
No open bead in the evidence is assigned to strachan or to anderson
The reply ties who got what to the workers' specialities (shown or stated: each bead's repo label matching its worker), and says Strachan is still idle

evals.name: dispatch-fall-through
evals.prompt: You are anderson, the dispatcher seat of this Wheelhouse. Dispatch the ready work to the workers.
evals.expected_output: Dalglish, the only repo:ynh specialist, is busy on "Rework ynh delegate resolution". The ready P0 "Fix the ynh install crash on an empty manifest" (repo:ynh) falls through to Strachan, the idle general-purpose worker. McCoist (repo:ynm only) gets nothing, though it comes first in the roster.
assertions: In the evidence, "Fix the ynh install crash on an empty manifest" has assignee strachan
No bead in the evidence is newly assigned to mccoist or to anderson, and "Rework ynh delegate resolution" is still dalglish's, in progress
The reply says the ynh specialist (Dalglish) is busy, so the bead went to the general-purpose worker

evals.name: dispatch-fall-back
evals.prompt: You are anderson, the dispatcher seat of this Wheelhouse. Dispatch the ready work to the workers.
evals.expected_output: No worker has repo:ynr as a speciality. The ready "Add a status command to ynr" (repo:ynr) falls back to Strachan, the general-purpose worker, not to Dalglish (repo:ynh) or McCoist (repo:ynm), though Dalglish comes first in the roster.
assertions: In the evidence, "Add a status command to ynr" has assignee strachan
No bead in the evidence is assigned to dalglish, mccoist or anderson
The reply says no worker has repo:ynr as a speciality, so the general-purpose worker took it

evals.name: dispatch-no-general
evals.prompt: You are anderson, the dispatcher seat of this Wheelhouse. Dispatch the ready work to the workers.
evals.expected_output: Both workers are specialists: Dalglish (repo:ynh) and McCoist (repo:ynm). The ready "Add a status command to ynr" (repo:ynr) has nobody who can take it, so it stays unassigned. Reports that, and that the Wheelhouse should have a general-purpose worker (ask the desk to seat one).
assertions: In the evidence, "Add a status command to ynr" is unassigned
No bead in the evidence is assigned to dalglish, mccoist or anderson
The reply says nobody can take the ynr bead, and that the Wheelhouse needs a general-purpose worker (or one for repo:ynr)

evals.name: next-own-speciality
evals.prompt: You are mccoist, a worker seat of this Wheelhouse. What's next for you? Pick it up.
evals.expected_output: McCoist's speciality is repo:ynm, and nothing is assigned to it. Of the ready unassigned beads, it claims "Make ynm recall honour --limit" (repo:ynm, P2), as mccoist, and leaves the more urgent "Fix the ynh install crash on an empty manifest" (repo:ynh, P0) for the dispatcher.
assertions: In the evidence, "Make ynm recall honour --limit" has assignee mccoist and is in progress
In the evidence, "Fix the ynh install crash on an empty manifest" is still open and unassigned
The reply says it took the ynm bead and left the ynh one because that one isn't its speciality (or isn't its to take)

evals.name: inbox-assign-merge
evals.prompt: You are dalglish. The pull request for the ynh 0.13 changelog, https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12, has to be merged before I can go on, and only a human can merge it. Get it to them.
evals.expected_output: Uses the inbox (bash scripts/inbox.sh assign) to create a bead for the default human, Rook, looked up from the roster: titled for merging the changelog pull request, created as dalglish, with https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12 as its external_ref, blocking dalglish's own bead "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog". It does not merge the pull request itself, and does not assign the bead to a seat or to a person not in the roster.
assertions: In the evidence, there is a new bead about merging the changelog pull request, assigned to rook (the default human), with created_by dalglish
That bead's external_ref is https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12
In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" waits on that new bead
No bead is assigned to anyone who is neither a seat nor a human in the roster
The stubbed calls include no gh pr merge
The reply names the pull request by its short form as a Markdown link, such as [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12), not as a bare #12 or a bare URL

evals.name: inbox-merge-needs-url
evals.prompt: You are dalglish. The changelog pull request needs a human to merge it. Put it in their inbox.
evals.expected_output: Tries the inbox's assign, or reads its help, and finds that a merge needs the pull request's URL. No URL is known, so it creates no merge bead without one, and asks for the pull request's URL (or says it couldn't find one) rather than inventing one.
assertions: In the evidence, no bead about merging has an empty external_ref: either none was created, or the one created carries a real pull request URL the run found (not an invented one)
The reply says the merge needs the pull request's URL, and asks for it or says none was found
The reply does not claim the merge request is in the inbox unless the evidence shows a bead for it with a URL

evals.name: inbox-note
evals.prompt: You are anderson. Let the humans know, just so they know, that McCoist is off the rota until Monday and Dalglish has the release work. There's nothing for them to do.
evals.expected_output: Leaves an inbox note, not a bead: bash scripts/inbox.sh note, which calls ynm remember in the default human's namespace, human/rook, tagged inbox, saying McCoist is off until Monday and Dalglish has the release work. Creates no bead for it.
assertions: The stubbed calls include a ynm remember with namespace human/rook and the tag inbox, whose content mentions McCoist being off and Dalglish having the release work
In the evidence, no new bead was created for the note (only the four release beads exist)
The memory was not written in a seat's namespace (such as seat/anderson)

evals.name: inbox-register
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk of this Wheelhouse. Hi, it's me, Pat.
evals.expected_output: Registers Pat as a human with bash scripts/inbox.sh register: the roster's humans gain Pat, command pat, with git's email pat@example.com and pronouns they/them, beside Rook, still the only default human. Pat is not added to seats. Says Pat now has an inbox of their own.
assertions: In the evidence, the roster's humans include Pat with command pat and email pat@example.com, and not marked default
Rook is still in humans, and still the only one with default true
Pat is not in the roster's seats (the evidence's humans list is separate; no seat named Pat was made)
The reply tells Pat they are registered, or have an inbox of their own now

evals.name: inbox-show-known
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk of this Wheelhouse. What's waiting for the humans?
evals.expected_output: Runs bash scripts/inbox.sh show (or reads the same from the graph and ynm). Git's email is Pat's, so it shows Pat's own inbox first: the decision on dropping Go 1.24, asked by gahan. Then Rook's, the default human's, for anyone: the merge of [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12), asked by dalglish, which unblocks one bead, and anderson's note that McCoist is off until Monday.
assertions: The reply shows Pat's own inbox, with the decision on dropping Go 1.24 asked by gahan
The reply shows the default human Rook's inbox (for anyone), with the merge of the changelog asked by dalglish
The merge is named by its short form as a Markdown link to https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12, such as [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12)
The reply says the merge unblocks one bead (or the changelog)
The reply includes anderson's note that McCoist is off until Monday
Nothing was changed: the evidence shows the same beads, open, with the same assignees

evals.name: inbox-show-unknown
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk of this Wheelhouse. What's waiting for the humans?
evals.expected_output: Git's email (sam@example.com) matches no human, so it shows only the default human Rook's inbox: the merge of [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12) and anderson's note. It does not show Pat's decision as the reader's own, and invites the person to say who they are ("it's me, <name>") to get an inbox of their own.
assertions: The reply shows Rook's inbox: the merge of the changelog and the note about McCoist
The reply does not present Pat's decision as the reader's own inbox
The reply invites the person at the desk to say who they are, such as "it's me, <name>", to get their own inbox
The roster's humans are unchanged in the evidence: Rook and Pat only, nobody registered unasked

evals.name: needs-a-merge
evals.prompt: You are dalglish. The ynh 0.13 changelog is written and its pull request, https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12, is open, but you can't merge it yourself and the tag waits on it. Sort out what happens next in the work graph.
evals.expected_output: Doesn't merge, and doesn't wait silently. Assigns a bead for the merge to the default human, Rook, with the inbox script (bash scripts/inbox.sh assign --to default --url https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12 --blocks <its changelog bead>), created as dalglish, so its own changelog bead waits on the merge. It names the pull request as [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12) in its reply.
assertions: In the evidence, a bead about merging the pull request is assigned to rook, with created_by dalglish and external_ref https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12
In the evidence, "Write the ynh 0.13 changelog" waits on that merge bead
The stubbed calls include no gh pr merge
No bead is assigned to a name that is neither a seat nor a human in the roster
The reply names the pull request by its short form as a Markdown link, not as a bare #12 or a bare URL
